topic: PDS (no-linkage) sag targets and how to read free sag
statement: A tuner's targets for the no-linkage KTM rear end with 13.2 in of travel: 105-110 mm of rider sag and 25-40 mm of free (static) sag. Set rider sag first, then check free sag with the same measuring points: if free sag ends up below the range the spring is too soft for the rider (it needed too much preload), and if it is above the range the spring is too stiff. Before measuring, check the shock and its heim joints move freely.

Magazine testers disliked the stock feel of the WP 4CS fork on the 2014-2016 SX-F models and had the forks revalved by the fork maker's own service arm, with no hardware changes. After several rounds (the first settings were too stiff) the result was plush early in the stroke, controlled in the middle and resistant to bottoming, for about $275 plus oil. A local-racer valving and a supercross valving were both offered; service centres use their own valving specs.

source.name: Motocross Action - WP Factory Services 4CS fork mod

topic: AER 48 air fork: finding your pressure (450 SX-F)
statement: For the AER 48 fork on the 2017-1/2 450 SX-F the manual pressure is 156 psi. Magazine testers ran about 135 psi for novices, 145 for intermediates and 150 for experts. To find your own: start at the manual pressure and drop 2 psi at a time until the fork uses nearly all its travel without bottoming, with about 1.5 in left on a zip-tie on the leg. Set pressure first, then the compression clicker; their baseline was 15 clicks out on compression and rebound with the legs at the third line. Pressure rises with air temperature and by about 4 psi over a long moto, so reset it between motos and bleed the outer chambers regularly. Light or slow riders may need 10 cc or more less oil in the damping leg to reach full travel.

source.name: Motocross Action - WP AER air fork pressure on a 2017-1/2 Factory Edition

topic: 2017 Mikuni jetting and the jet-kit fix
statement: The Mikuni carburettor on the 2017 KTM-family two-strokes is rich off the bottom and uneven elsewhere as delivered, going lean, rich and lean again as the power valve moves, and it is sensitive to the premix ratio. An aftermarket jet kit tested on a 2017 300 XC-W (two multi-taper needles, a half-clip washer, mains and pilots and a chart by altitude, temperature and riding style, about $85) gave steadier throttle response, slightly more power, about five more miles per tank on the trail setting and jetting that held across temperature and elevation. The richer race needle reduced detonation. Kits are specific to the bike and year: the 2018 engines use a different needle jet.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test - high performance Mikuni jet kit for KTM
